breakfast.name: Desayuno Chapín
instructions: Fry eggs, fry plantain slices
Warm refried beans and tortillas
Plate together with cheese and salsa
breakfast.description: The Guatemalan breakfast — beans, eggs, plantain, cheese, and tortillas.

breakfast.name: Champurradas (Sugar-Topped Cookies)
instructions: Cream butter and sugar, add eggs
Mix in flour
Shape cookies, press sesame seeds on top
Bake at 175°C 15 min
breakfast.description: Crunchy sugar cookies with sesame — served with coffee.

breakfast.name: Desayuno Chapín (Full Guatemalan Breakfast)
instructions: Fry or scramble eggs
Warm refried black beans — they should be creamy and smooth
Fry ripe plantain slices until golden and caramelized
Warm tortillas on a comal
Arrange on plate: eggs, beans, plantain, cheese, cream
Roll beans and egg in a tortilla for a quick taco, or eat each component separately
Black coffee on the side — Guatemala grows excellent coffee
This is the standard Guatemalan morning — every component is essential
breakfast.description: Guatemala's complete breakfast — refried black beans, eggs, fried plantain, fresh cream, cheese, and handmade tortillas. Every element is simple but together they're perfect. The morning tortilla-making ritual and the Guatemalan coffee (from one of the world's best coffee regions) make this a viral Central American breakfast.

breakfast.name: Rellenitos (Stuffed Plantain Balls)
ingredients: 1 cup refried black beans (sweet version, with sugar and cinnamon)
instructions: Boil ripe plantains until very tender, mash smooth
Form into balls with a hollow center
Fill each with a spoonful of sweetened, chocolate-spiked black beans
Close the plantain around the filling, reshape into an oval
Fry until golden and crispy outside — 3-4 min
Roll in cinnamon sugar while warm
The contrast: sweet crispy plantain shell, chocolate-bean filling inside
These are Guatemala's unique sweet — nothing else in the world is quite like them
breakfast.description: Guatemala's most unique sweet — fried plantain balls stuffed with chocolate-spiked sweetened black beans, rolled in cinnamon sugar. The concept of 'chocolate beans inside fried plantain' blows people's minds. Rellenitos are uniquely Guatemalan and the cross-section reveal is always viral.

lunch.name: Pepián (Meat Stew)
instructions: Toast seeds, chiles, spices, tomatoes, tomatillos
Blend into thick sauce
Brown meats
Add sauce, simmer 45 min
Thicken with toasted tortilla
Serve with rice
lunch.description: Guatemala's national dish — a rich, ancient Mayan meat stew.

lunch.name: Kak'ik (Turkey Soup)
instructions: Toast chiles, tomatoes, tomatillos
Blend sauce
Simmer turkey in sauce 45 min
Add cilantro and mint
Serve with rice and tamales
lunch.description: Ancient Q'eqchi' Mayan turkey soup — red and aromatic.

lunch.name: Pepián (Guatemala's National Stew)
ingredients: Chicken or pork (bone-in, cut into pieces)
Pepián paste: dried guajillo and pasilla chilies, tomatoes, tomatillos, pepitoria (roasted pumpkin seeds), sesame seeds, cinnamon, cloves, black pepper
Vegetables: chayote, green beans, potatoes, carrots
instructions: Toast dried chilies on a dry comal until fragrant — do not burn
Roast tomatoes, tomatillos on the comal
Toast pumpkin seeds and sesame seeds
Toast corn tortillas until crispy
Blend everything: chilies, tomatoes, tomatillos, seeds, tortillas, spices into a thick paste
Brown meat, add pepián paste, dilute with stock
Add vegetables — root vegetables first
Simmer 45-60 min until meat is tender and sauce is thick
The sauce should coat the back of a spoon — rich, dark, nutty
Serve with rice and tortillas
lunch.description: Guatemala's national dish — a thick, seed-and-chili stew with pre-Columbian Mayan roots. The toasted pumpkin seed and sesame base creates a rich, nutty sauce unlike any other in Central America. Pepián connects modern Guatemala directly to its Mayan culinary heritage. The ancient-technique story and the complex seed paste are viral.

lunch.name: Kak'ik (Turkey Soup — Mayan Ceremonial)
ingredients: Whole turkey (cut into pieces) or turkey legs
instructions: Toast dried chilies on comal
Blend chilies with tomatoes, tomatillos, achiote paste, toasted pumpkin seeds, herbs
Cook turkey in water until tender — reserve the broth
Add the blended chili-seed paste to the broth
Simmer until sauce is thick and deeply red from the achiote
The color should be a vibrant red-orange — the achiote is both color and flavor
Add masa to thicken further if needed
Return turkey to the soup
Serve in deep bowls with rice and tortillas
This is a Mayan ceremonial dish — still served at important gatherings and holidays
UNESCO recognized Kak'ik as Intangible Cultural Heritage of Guatemala
lunch.description: Guatemala's Mayan ceremonial turkey soup — red from achiote, thickened with pumpkin seeds, and recognized by UNESCO as Intangible Cultural Heritage. This recipe connects directly to pre-Columbian Mayan feasts. The UNESCO status and the living Mayan tradition make Kak'ik one of Central America's most culturally significant and viral dishes.

lunch.name: Hilachas (Shredded Beef in Tomato-Tomatillo Sauce)
ingredients: Sauce: tomatoes, tomatillos, guaque chilies, garlic
instructions: Boil beef until tender enough to shred — 1+ hours
Shred beef finely — 'hilachas' means 'threads' or 'rags'
Toast and blend chilies, tomatoes, tomatillos, garlic into a smooth sauce
Fry the sauce until thick and dark
Add shredded beef, potatoes, carrots
Simmer until vegetables are tender and sauce clings to the meat
The shredded meat should be so fine it looks like threads
Serve with rice and tortillas
lunch.description: Guatemala's 'rags' — beef shredded so finely it looks like threads, simmered in a tomato-tomatillo-chili sauce. The name 'hilachas' (rags/threads) comes from the ultra-fine shredding technique. The thread-like meat texture and the rich sauce have made this a viral Guatemalan comfort food.

dinner.name: Hilachas (Shredded Beef in Sauce)
instructions: Boil beef until tender, shred
Blend tomatoes, tomatillos, chile, onion, garlic
Cook sauce, add beef, potatoes, carrots
Simmer 20 min
Serve with rice and tortillas
dinner.description: Shredded beef in smooth tomato-chile sauce.

dinner.name: Chiles Rellenos (Stuffed Peppers)
ingredients: Filling: ground pork, raisins, capers, olives
instructions: Roast and peel peppers
Fill with pork mixture
Dip in egg batter, fry
Serve in tomato recado sauce
dinner.description: Stuffed peppers in egg batter with tomato sauce.

dinner.name: Tamales Colorados (Red Tamales)
ingredients: Masa: corn masa harina, lard or butter, tomato-chili recado (for the red color)
Filling: chicken or pork, recado rojo (achiote-tomato paste), olives, capers, prunes, red pepper
Wrapping: banana leaves (not corn husks — Central American style)
Recado: tomatoes, achiote, pepitoria, sesame seeds, dried chilies
instructions: Make recado: toast and blend chilies, tomatoes, achiote, pumpkin seeds, sesame — a thick, red paste
Cook meat in recado until tender, shred
Mix recado into masa with lard — the masa turns red
Soften banana leaves over flame — they become pliable
Spread red masa on banana leaf, add meat filling, olives, capers, prune
Fold banana leaf into a neat rectangle, tie with string
Steam for 1.5 hours until masa is firm and pulls away from the leaf
The red color from the recado is the signature — not like Mexican green or plain tamales
These are Saturday and Christmas food — making tamales is a family event that takes all day
A proper Guatemalan tamale is the size of a brick — much bigger than Mexican tamales
dinner.description: Guatemala's red tamales — masa dyed red with a toasted chili-seed paste, filled with chicken, olives, capers, and prunes, wrapped in banana leaves. Brick-sized and labor-intensive, making tamales is a family-wide Saturday or Christmas event. The red color, the banana-leaf unwrap, and the sweet-savory olive-prune filling are viral.

dinner.name: Chiles Rellenos (Stuffed Peppers Guatemalan Style)
ingredients: Filling: pork picadillo (ground pork with tomato, onion, raisins, olives, capers)
Egg batter: eggs separated, whites whipped stiff
instructions: Roast peppers, peel, remove seeds — keep whole
Make picadillo: cook ground pork with tomato, onion, raisins, olives, capers — the sweet-savory mix is the point
Stuff peppers with picadillo
Dust stuffed peppers in flour
Make egg batter: beat whites stiff, fold in yolks
Dip floured, stuffed peppers in batter — coat completely
Fry until golden on all sides — the egg batter puffs into a golden cloud
Serve in tomato sauce
The puffy egg coating is the Guatemalan signature — different from Mexican dried chili versions
dinner.description: Guatemalan stuffed peppers — filled with sweet-savory picadillo (pork, raisins, olives, capers) and coated in a puffy whipped egg batter that fries into a golden cloud. The egg-cloud technique distinguishes Guatemala's version from Mexican chiles rellenos and the puff-and-slice moment is viral.

snacks.name: Rellenitos de Plátano
instructions: Boil plantains, mash
Fill with refried beans and cinnamon
Shape into ovals
Fry until golden
Dust with sugar
snacks.description: Sweet plantain ovals stuffed with black beans.

snacks.name: Chuchitos (Small Tamales)
ingredients: Filling: tomato-based chicken or pork recado
Corn husks (unlike big tamales, chuchitos use corn husks)
instructions: Mix masa with lard and salt until light and fluffy
Spread on softened corn husks
Add a spoonful of tomato-chicken filling
Fold corn husk around, tie
Steam 35-40 min until firm
The difference from regular tamales: chuchitos are small, use corn husks, and are simpler
Serve with tomato salsa or curtido (cabbage slaw)
Chuchitos are street food — sold from carts at any hour
snacks.description: Guatemala's street tamale — smaller and simpler than the grand tamal colorado, wrapped in corn husks instead of banana leaves. Sold from carts at every corner. The grab-and-go format and the tomato salsa drizzle make chuchitos Guatemala's most accessible and viral street snack.

snacks.name: Tostadas Guatemaltecas
instructions: Fry corn tortillas flat until crispy and golden — they must shatter slightly when bitten
Spread with refried black beans
Top with guacamole
Add salsa and shredded chicken if desired
Sprinkle queso fresco and curtido on top
The architecture matters — each layer should be visible
Eat with both hands, biting from the edge — some breakage is expected and acceptable
snacks.description: Guatemalan tostadas — crispy fried tortillas stacked with beans, guacamole, salsa, and cheese. The satisfying crunch and the layered architecture make tostadas viral street food content. The inevitable messy collapse when you bite in is part of the charm.

snacks.name: Tostadas Guatemaltecas
instructions: Spread black bean paste on tostada
Top with guacamole
Add salsa, crumbled queso fresco, curtido
Garnish with radish slices
The contrast of textures: crispy tostada, creamy bean, crunchy curtido
Eat in 3-4 bites — it's a one-hand snack
Tostadas are Guatemala's answer to the open-faced sandwich — every market has them
The stack of toppings on the flat tortilla is a perfect flavor delivery system
snacks.description: Guatemalan tostadas — crispy flat tortillas stacked with black bean paste, guacamole, salsa, and pickled cabbage. Every market has a tostada vendor. The one-handed, multi-textured, flavor-stacked concept makes tostadas a perpetually viral Latin American street food.

snacks.name: Chuchitos (Guatemalan Tamales)
instructions: Make masa dough — slightly wetter than tortilla masa
Make filling: chicken or pork cooked in tomato-recado salsa
Spread masa on corn husk — not banana leaf (that's for the larger tamales)
Add filling, fold corn husk to enclose
Steam 25-30 min until masa is firm
Chuchitos are smaller than ceremonial tamales — everyday tamales
The corn husk wrapper is the distinction — banana leaf wrapping is for special occasions
Serve with additional salsa on top
The name 'chuchitos' is a Guatemalan diminutive — 'little dogs' — affectionate naming for food
snacks.description: Guatemala's everyday tamale — smaller than the ceremonial version, wrapped in corn husk instead of banana leaf, filled with chicken in tomato-recado salsa. Called chuchitos ('little dogs') with typical Guatemalan affection for food naming.

desserts.name: Buñuelos de Viento
instructions: Make choux-style dough
Drop into hot oil, fry until puffed and golden
Drizzle with honey syrup and cinnamon
desserts.description: Airy fried dough puffs in cinnamon-honey syrup.

desserts.name: Buñuelos con Miel (Fried Dough with Honey Syrup)
ingredients: Dough: flour, eggs, butter, anise, baking powder
instructions: Make dough with flour, eggs, butter, anise — rest 20 min
Roll thin, cut into rounds
Deep fry until golden and puffy — 2-3 min
Make miel: dissolve panela in water with cinnamon — simmer until thick syrup
Drizzle hot syrup over fried buñuelos
The crispy exterior soaks up the sweet, cinnamon-infused panela syrup
Served at Christmas and Semana Santa (Holy Week) — Guatemala's holiday sweet
The syrup-pouring moment over the stack of buñuelos is the show
desserts.description: Guatemala's holiday fried dough — thin, crispy rounds drenched in dark panela-cinnamon syrup. Essential at Christmas and Semana Santa. The dramatic syrup-pour over a pyramid of buñuelos and the sticky, sweet result are peak Guatemalan holiday food content.

desserts.name: Champurradas (Guatemalan Sugar Cookies)
instructions: Cream butter and sugar
Add eggs, vanilla
Mix in flour, baking powder
Shape into thick, round cookies
Top generously with sesame seeds — pressed into the surface
Bake at 175°C for 12-15 min until firm and lightly golden
Not soft and chewy — champurradas are meant to be crunchy and dunkable
Serve with coffee or hot chocolate — dunking is the ritual
Every Guatemalan bakery has a jar of champurradas by the register
desserts.description: Guatemala's crunchy sesame-topped cookies — designed for dunking into coffee or hot chocolate. Found in every bakery, bought by the bag. The sesame coating and the dunking ritual connect champurradas to Guatemala's exceptional coffee culture.

desserts.name: Rellenitos de Plátano (Stuffed Plantain)
instructions: Boil ripe plantains until very soft, mash
Make sweetened black bean paste — cook black beans with sugar and cinnamon until thick
Take a portion of mashed plantain, flatten in palm
Add a spoonful of sweet bean paste in the center
Close the plantain around the filling — shape into an oval
Fry in oil until golden on all sides
The sweet plantain shell and the sweet-spiced bean filling are both sweet — double sweet
Dust with sugar if desired
These are Guatemala's most beloved sweet — the bean-and-plantain pairing is genius
desserts.description: Guatemalan rellenitos — mashed ripe plantain stuffed with sweetened cinnamon black beans and fried. The double-sweet pairing of sweet plantain and sweet beans sounds unusual but is genius. Rellenitos are Guatemala's most beloved homemade sweet and a viral discovery for first-timers.

drinks.name: Rosa de Jamaica (Hibiscus Tea)
instructions: Boil hibiscus 10 min
Strain, sweeten
Add lime, serve cold

drinks.name: Atol de Elote
instructions: Cut corn from cob, blend with milk
Strain through sieve
Cook with sugar and cinnamon until thick
Serve warm

drinks.name: Atol de Elote (Sweet Corn Drink)
ingredients: 6 ears fresh sweet corn (kernels cut off)
instructions: Blend corn kernels with milk until smooth
Strain through a fine sieve — or leave unstrained for thicker version
Cook in a pot with sugar, cinnamon, vanilla, stirring constantly
Simmer until thick and creamy — 15-20 min
The fresh corn flavor should be prominent — not just sweetness, but corniness
Serve hot or warm in mugs
This is a seasonal drink — made when fresh corn is in season
The natural sweetness and creaminess from the corn need minimal added sugar
drinks.description: Guatemala's fresh corn drink — sweet corn kernels blended with milk and cinnamon into a thick, warm, creamy beverage. Seasonal and irreplaceable (you need fresh corn). The natural corn sweetness and the hot-drink comfort factor make atol de elote viral during corn season across Central America.

drinks.name: Atol de Elote (Fresh Corn Drink)
instructions: Cut corn from cobs — must be fresh, not canned
Blend corn with milk until smooth
Strain through a sieve — push through as much as possible
Heat the strained mixture with sugar, cinnamon, vanilla
Stir constantly — it thickens as it heats
Cook 15-20 min until the consistency of thick hot chocolate
The corn flavor should be sweet, milky, and warm
Serve hot — this is Guatemala's comfort drink for cold highland evenings
The fresh corn taste in a warm drink is unlike anything else
drinks.description: Guatemalan atol de elote — fresh sweet corn blended with milk and cinnamon into a thick, warm drink. A highland Guatemala comfort on cold evenings. The 'corn as a warm drink' concept surprises and delights first-time tasters and goes viral every time.
